rows.text: Charged $14.99 to Morgan's card, paid to Nomiq Domains.

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for reaching out. I'm afraid I can't provide a quote for this piece right now — I need to have a conversation with my employer before doing any public statements about Halcyon Threshold. I'd be happy to talk once that's resolved, likely in a week or two. Feel free to reach out again then if it's still relevant for future coverage. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Declined reporter quote (can't do public statements yet)

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — that's incredibly generous and I'd love to take you up on it. The most useful thing right now would be research to help identify neglected areas. Specifically: what aspects of advanced AI systems are *not* being systematically evaluated or measured by any major lab, research org, or eval group? This could involve: - Reviewing public eval suites and research agendas from labs (Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepMind, etc.) - Checking what independent orgs are measuring (METR, Apollo, etc.) - Identifying capability or safety dimensions that seem overlooked The goal would be a short document (even just a structured list) of gaps that could inform where Halcyon Threshold focuses. Does that sound interesting? No pressure if it's not the kind of work you were thinking of. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Accepted Priya Raman's help - asked her to research neglected eval areas

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Sam Whitlock <sam@whitlock.dev> with subject "Question about eval gaps". It read: "Hi Sam, We met at the meetup last week — I'm working on Halcyon Threshold, focused on contributing to good outcomes for superintelligence. You mentioned you do independent evals work. I'm trying to identify what's genuinely neglected in the evaluation space — capabilities or safety properties that aren't being systematically measured by any lab or research org. Do you have a sense of what the biggest gaps are? Or what you wish existed but doesn't? Would appreciate any quick thoughts. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Reached out to Sam (indie evals) and Asha (forum) for input on gaps

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Asha Venkataraman <asha.v@alignmentcommons.org> with subject "Looking for input on neglected work". It read: "Hi Asha, We met online a while back through the forum. I'm working on Halcyon Threshold — trying to figure out where a small independent project could contribute most effectively to AI safety. You see a lot of what people are working on through the forum. What areas seem genuinely neglected or underfunded? What do you wish more people were doing? Any quick thoughts would be really helpful. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Reached out to Sam (indie evals) and Asha (forum) for input on gaps

rows.text: Published the public website at halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app.

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Hi, Thanks for the invitation to sign. I support the goals but need to decline for now — I need to complete my employer's outside-activities disclosure process before making public statements in a professional capacity. I'd be happy to consider signing similar letters in the future once that's resolved. Best, Morgan Hale"
